text:
anya: quick async check — wrapping up the prefetch/warmup sprint items. posting owners, blockers, and a couple small asks. TL;DR: prefetch lag down to ~12ms median on canary, still seeing sporadic cold misses on >1024 tokens workloads.

matt: great, can you paste the canary job id and the specific test that showed 12ms? want to link to perf dashboard.

anya: canary job id: canary-prefetch-2026-03-10-17, test is `warmup-window-1k-seq` (10k samples). dashboard: https://internal.redwood.com/dashboards/prefetch-canny (perm link)

sanjay: saw the same run. congrats on the median. note: p95 is still ~72ms which correlates with the eviction path we discussed. I believe it's the LRU bump on the 40% traffic slice.

oliver: ownership recap: prefetch algorithm - anya; cache eviction & metrics - sanjay; kernel hook changes - matt; rollout automation - jin. correct?

anya: yep. addition: infra change (larger mmap limit) was done by jin last week and helped reduce OOMs in canary. jin: can you confirm the exact change and whether it's safe for prod?

jin: changed vm.max_map_count to 262144 on canary hosts (ansible id: infra-2026-03-05). safe to prod after a quick infra runbook update. will open a small PR to ops playbooks.

matt: blockers: i still need two quick CRs for the kernel hook that skips the KV lookup on small prefixes. @oliver can you review? it's tiny.

oliver: will review today EOD. if it's small i'll merge. also left a comment about naming in the tests.

anya: dependency status: rollout depends on two things — 1) jin finishing the runbook + prod vm change, 2) matt's CR merged. after that we can flip prefetch warmup for 10% of traffic.

sanjay: operational concern: when we flip to 10%, watch our trace ingest. the new metrics tag `prefetch_v2` isn't in trace sampling yet, so we might miss early signals. can we add a lightweight log line?

jin: i can add the tag to the trace sampler quickly. PR: infra/trace#412. should be low-risk.

anya: asks for the next 24h: (1) matt - CR review + merge; (2) jin - runbook PR + trace tag prod flip; (3) oliver - merge naming fix; (4) sanjay - prepare alert threshold suggestions for p95 and error budget impact.

matt: confirming i'll do the CR today. i also want to sanity-check the microbatching knobs — we saw a small regression at 4-token batches in a subset of runs. that's a follow-up, not blocking.

oliver: merged naming fix, CI passed.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary-prefetch-2026-03-10-17 started by matt at 2026-03-10T18:03:12Z

sanjay: i'll draft alert thresholds and post later tonight. proposing p95 alert at 120ms, p99 at 400ms for warmup window, and a soft signal for cold-miss-rate > 0.5%.

anya: thanks. one more note: i've added a short eval prompt set to detect quality regressions after prefetch kicks in (folder: /evals/prefetch-warmup/). want to avoid any hallucination regressions from cache priming.

matt: thanks — please ping me if any eval shows rerank drops.

anya: final: tentative rollout plan in ops doc: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 48 hours with immediate rollback on error_budget_breach or cold-miss-rate spike. posting doc link: https://internal.redwood.com/ops/prefetch-rollout.

oliver: sounds good. i'll check the rollout automation to ensure the canary group sizes match.

jin: runbook PR opened: infra/runbooks#227. includes vm change steps and rollback notes.

matt: merged kernel hook CR. will watch canary for 2 hours, then we can do the 10% flip if jin's infra PR is green.

anya: thank you all. i'll schedule a short sync if anything weird pops up. otherwise i'll post final status after 10% flip. :thumbsup:

oliver: (reaction :eyes:)

sanjay: will post alert thresholds in ~3h.

anja: (typo) meant to say "anya" — all good :)
